paper.title: May the Forque Be with You: Dynamics in PGA

conventions.note: their code index 0 is our bit 0, so mask 0b1111 is e0123

conventions.ours: bits 1..d, square +1 ("time-type" in the atlas rule)
conventions.note: the atlas rule has space squares -1; the whole dynamics also runs with sq = [0, -1, ..., -1] (law of motion checked in d = 2, 3), the energy then changes sign

conventions.ours: XOR of masks with the sign of the bit rule
conventions.note: e31 = -mask 0b1010 (ours is ascending), e032 = -mask 0b1101, e021 = -mask 0b0111; the renderer prints the paper's names

conventions.theirs: O = e1 ... ed,  I = eps O,  Q = O + q I
conventions.ours: O = mask of bits 1..d; I = eps * O

conventions.theirs: plane p = n - delta eps; translation T = 1 - eps t/2; X -> M X M~
conventions.note: their eps is minus the eps of [13] v < 2.0; we use the current one throughout

conventions.theirs: x . A = (x A - A^ x)/2;  A x B = (A B - B A)/2
conventions.note: x . A is the left contraction of a vector

conventions.theirs: Hodge star: X (*X) = X X~_E I
conventions.note: reproduces *O = eps, *(q I) = q, *E = -E I, *(eps e_k) = e_k I_d (F00); *^-1 is the inverse on masks

conventions.theirs: motors exp(-B t/2); B_w = -2 Mdot M~; B_b = -2 M~ Mdot
conventions.ours: ser_exp(B, -1/2); exact power series in t
conventions.note: no floating point anywhere in the exact rows

rows.paper: \star O=\epsilon,\ \ \star(\mathbf q\mathcal I)=\mathbf q,\ \ \star\mathbf E=-\mathbf E\mathcal I,\ \ \star(\epsilon\mathbf e_k)=\mathbf e_k\mathbf I_d
rows.how: the star as signed complement; the four values the paper states are reproduced in d = 2, 3, 4; join = *^-1(*A ^ *B)

rows.paper: p=\mathbf n-\delta\epsilon,\ \ (1-\epsilon\mathbf q/2)\,\mathbf n\,(1+\epsilon\mathbf q/2)=\mathbf n-(\mathbf q\cdot\mathbf n)\epsilon
rows.how: random n, q; both signs of the orientation of eps respected (eps^2 = 0, n eps = - eps n)

rows.paper: Q=(1-\epsilon\mathbf q/2)\,O\,(1+\epsilon\mathbf q/2)=(1-\epsilon\mathbf q)O=O+\mathbf q\mathcal I,\ \ \mathcal I=\epsilon O
rows.ours: Q = T O \tilde T = O + q\,(\epsilon O)
rows.how: translation of O; (1 - eps q) O; point split from another centre C; I = eps Q for every point Q

rows.paper: Q=(\mathbf e_1-q_1\epsilon)\wedge\dots\wedge(\mathbf e_d-q_d\epsilon)
rows.how: a point is the meet of d planes

rows.paper: V_{\mathbf u}=\mathbf u\mathcal I\ \ (\text{a point without an }O\text{ part})
rows.how: V is translation invariant; Q + t V_u is the point moved by t u

rows.paper: L_o=O\vee(O+\mathbf u\mathcal I)=O\vee(\mathbf u\mathcal I)=\mathbf u\cdot O
rows.how: join = *^-1(*A ^ *B), the star as above; the join of a point with itself vanishes

rows.paper: L=(1-\epsilon\mathbf q/2)(\mathbf u\cdot O)(1+\epsilon\mathbf q/2)=\mathbf u\cdot O+(\mathbf u\wedge\mathbf q)\mathcal I=\mathbf u\cdot Q
rows.ours: T(u\cdot O)\tilde T = u\cdot O + (u\wedge q)\,I = u\cdot Q
rows.how: where x.A = (xA - A^ x)/2 for a vector x

rows.paper: Q\vee(\mathbf u\mathcal I)=\mathbf u\cdot Q
rows.note: In d = 2, 3, 4 with the join of footnote 3 we find Q v (uI) = u.Q and O v (uI) = u.O with no (-1)^(d-1); that remark in 1.3.2 may belong to the older join convention.
rows.how: d = 2, 3, 4.  The remark after (1.5), "u.Q (-1)^(d-1) in R_{d,0,1}", does not appear: with the footnote-3 join the sign is +1 in every d we tried

rows.paper: \mathbf p\wedge(\mathbf u\cdot Q)=0\iff \mathbf p\wedge Q=0\ \text{and}\ \mathbf p\cdot\mathbf u=0
rows.how: planes through Q with a normal perpendicular to u lie in the pencil; a generic plane does not

rows.paper: \mathbb B=\mathbf B+\epsilon\mathbf v=\big(\mathbf B+\epsilon(\mathbf v\cdot\mathbf B)/\mathbf B\big)-\epsilon(\mathbf v\wedge\mathbf B)/\mathbf B=\omega L+\nu L\mathcal I
rows.note: Exact check: B = [B_E + eps (v.B_E)/B_E] + eps (v^B_E)/B_E, with a PLUS in front of the second term.  The printed final line has a minus there, which does not add up to B (the worked instance shows the plus version).
rows.how: the two parts commute and each is a 2-blade; a screw = a rotation about L together with a translation along it
rows.code: Bm + A.eps * (A.vdot(v, Bm) * Binv) + A.eps * (v.wedge(Bm) * Binv) == Bm + A.eps * v

rows.paper: \dot M=-\tfrac12\mathbb B M,\ \mathbb B=-2\dot M\widetilde M;\quad M=M_0e^{-\mathbb B_b t/2}:\ \dot M=-\tfrac12 M\mathbb B_b,\ \mathbb B_b=-2\widetilde M\dot M;\quad \mathbb B_w=M\mathbb B_b\widetilde M
rows.ours: dM/dt = -\tfrac12 B M,\ \ B = -2\,\dot M\,\tilde M
rows.how: exact power series in t through order 6: M = exp(-Bt/2) M0 and M0 exp(-B t/2); the two rates differ by M0 (the paradox) and agree only at M0 = 1

rows.paper: M\widetilde M=1\Rightarrow\dot M\widetilde M=-M\dot{\widetilde M};\ \ \mathbb B=-2\dot M\widetilde M\ \text{is a bivector}
rows.how: for a time-varying rate B(t): M solves Mdot = -B M/2; M M~ stays constant, -2 Mdot M~ returns B(t), and it has only grade 2

rows.paper: \dot X=X\times\mathbb B_w\ \ (X=MX_0\widetilde M);\qquad \dot X_w=X_w\times\mathbb B_w+M\dot X_b\widetilde M
rows.how: power series; X a point, a line and a plane; and a moving X_b (the extra term of 2.9)

rows.paper: \dot X=\dot{\mathbf x}\mathcal I=X\times\mathbb B_w,\ \ \dot{\mathbf x}=\mathbf v+\mathbf x\cdot\mathbf B
rows.how: x . e12 sends e1 to e2: the rate B = e12 is counter-clockwise, as the text says
rows.code: A.comm(Q, Bm + A.eps * v) == (v + A.vdot(q, Bm)) * A.I

rows.paper: M=e^{-\mathbf v_wt/2}M_0\ \Rightarrow\ \mathbb B_b=\widetilde M(\mathbf v_w)M=\epsilon\,\widetilde R\mathbf v_wR\neq0
rows.how: a translation seen in the body frame is not zero: ideal elements are part of the body frame ("share your ideals")
rows.code: M0.rev() * (A.eps * u) * M0 == A.eps * (R3.rev() * u * R3)

rows.paper: P\equiv mX\vee\dot X=mX\vee(\dot{\mathbf x}\mathcal I)=m\dot{\mathbf x}\cdot X
rows.ours: P = m\,\mathrm{join}(X, \dot x I) = m\,\dot x\cdot X
rows.how: the join line is unchanged by sliding the point along the line (gauge freedom)

rows.paper: P=m\mathbf v\cdot Y+m\mathbf v\cdot(X-Y)=m\mathbf v\cdot Y-(\mathbf r\wedge m\mathbf v)\mathcal I
rows.ours: m\,v\cdot X = m\,v\cdot Y - m\,((x-y)\wedge v)\,I
rows.note: The displayed derivation is exact with X - Y = r I, i.e. r = x - y. The sentence just before it defines r = y - x, which would flip the sign of the last term.
rows.how: exact in d = 2, 3, 4 with r = x - y (the position of the mass seen from Y), so that in 3D the last term is eps (r x p), the classical angular momentum
rows.code: A.vdot(v, Q) == A.vdot(v, R) - A.vec([a - b for a, b in zip(ql, rl)]).wedge(v) * A.I

rows.paper: P=\sum_iP_i=\mathsf I_w[\mathbb B_w],\ \ \mathsf I_w[\mathbb B]=\sum_i m_iX_i\vee(X_i\times\mathbb B);\ \ \mathsf I_{X\cup Y}=\mathsf I_X+\mathsf I_Y
rows.how: each P_i is a blade; the total is a blade in 2D but generally not in 3D; the inertia of a union is the sum; I is linear

rows.paper: \mathsf I_b[\mathbb B_b]\equiv\widetilde M\,\mathsf I_w[M\mathbb B_b\widetilde M]\,M\ \ (\text{depends on the body only})
rows.ours: M^\sim I_w[M B M^\sim] M = I_b[B]
rows.how: random motor, body and rate; the world inertia is the body inertia moved by M

rows.paper: \mathsf I_b[\mathbf B+\epsilon\mathbf v]=m\,\mathbf v\cdot O-\mathsf I_C[\mathbf B]\,\mathcal I;\ \ \mathsf I_C[\mathbf B]=\sum_im_i\mathbf r_i\wedge(\mathbf r_i\cdot\mathbf B);\ \ \mathsf I_b^{-1}[\mathbf v\cdot O-\mathbf B\mathcal I]=\epsilon\mathbf v/m+\mathsf I_C^{-1}[\mathbf B]
rows.how: centroidal body; I_C is the classical GA inertia; exact in d = 2, 3, 4
rows.code: cb.I_def(Bm + A.eps * v) == A.vdot(v, A.O).scale(cb.m) - cb.IC(Bm) * A.I

rows.paper: \mathsf I_b[\sum_{ij}[\mathbb B]_{ij}\mathbf e_{ij}]=\sum\lambda_{ij}[\mathbb B]_{ij}\star\mathbf e_{ij},\ \ \lambda_{ij}=i_{ij}\ (i,j\ne0),\ m\ (i=0);\ \ \text{3D matrix }\begin{pmatrix}0&m\mathbb 1\\ \mathsf I_C&0\end{pmatrix}
rows.ours: I[e_{ij}] = i_{ij}\star e_{ij},\ \ I[\epsilon e_k] = m\star(\epsilon e_k)
rows.how: a body with principal axes along the coordinate axes; also the 6 x 6 matrix in the basis (e23, e31, e12, e01, e02, e03) and the inverse

rows.paper: \mathsf I_C[\mathbf B]'=\mathsf I_C[\mathbf B]+m\,\mathbf q\wedge(\mathbf q\cdot\mathbf B);\ \ \mathsf I_b[\mathbb T_q\mathbf B\widetilde{\mathbb T}_q]=-m(\mathbf q\cdot\mathbf B)\cdot Q-(\mathsf I_C[\mathbf B]+m\mathbf q\wedge(\mathbf q\cdot\mathbf B))\mathcal I
rows.ours: I[T B \tilde T] = -m((q\cdot B)\cdot Q) - (I_C[B] + m\,q\wedge(q\cdot B))\,I
rows.remark: Exact. The page also contains a leftover draft note: "[[[ but sdo we care how teh cetnroid moves? Should we not want Q? ]]]" (p. 65, in the point-split paragraph).
rows.how: no parallel-axis theorem: shifting the axis only changes the argument. The stray editing note inside p.65 ("[[[ but sdo we care ... ]]]") is still in the text of version 2.6

rows.paper: P=\mathbf p\cdot C-\mathbf L\mathcal I\ \ (\mathbf p=m\dot{\mathbf c},\ \mathbf L=\textstyle\sum m\,\mathbf r_i\wedge\dot{\mathbf r}_i)
rows.how: general rigid body, general rate; p and L are computed classically from the point velocities

rows.paper: F=Q\vee(\mathbf f\mathcal I)=\mathbf f\cdot Q=\mathbf f\cdot R-\mathbf T_R\mathcal I;\ \ F=\sum_i\mathbf f_i\cdot Q_i=\mathbf f\cdot O-\mathbf T_O\mathcal I
rows.ours: F = f\cdot Q = f\cdot R - T_R\,I,\quad T_R=(q-r)\wedge f
rows.note: Exact with T_R = (q - r) ^ f. On p.31 the line "T_R = (r - q) ^ f" has the opposite sign (it would also give T_R I = +tau instead of -tau). A.16 (T_O = sum q_i ^ f_i) is consistent with the corrected form.
rows.how: exact in d = 2, 3, 4; the torque is the 2-blade (q-r)^f, in 3D its dual is the classical torque
rows.code: A.vdot(f, Q) == A.vdot(f, R) - A.vec([a - b for a, b in zip(ql, rl)]).wedge(f) * A.I

rows.paper: \dot P=F;\ \ \mathsf I_b[\mathbb B]=\sum m_iX_i\vee(X_i\times\mathbb B);\ \ \dot{\mathbb B}_b=\mathsf I_b^{-1}[\mathbb B_b\times\mathsf I_b[\mathbb B_b]+F_b];\ \ \dot M=-\tfrac12M\mathbb B_b
rows.how: the state (M, B_b) is solved as an exact power series (Picard iteration) through order 7; the mass points move as X_i = M X_i^b M~; then d/dt sum m_i X_i v Xdot_i equals the sum of the forques, term by term, for no forque, gravity (2.31) and a Hooke spring. Negative controls: dropping B x I[B], flipping its sign, or dropping the 1/2 each break Pdot = F

rows.paper: T=\tfrac12\mathbb B_b\vee\mathsf I_b[\mathbb B_b],\ \ T\mathcal I=\tfrac12\mathbb B_b\wedge\mathsf I_b[\mathbb B_b];\quad \Pi=\mathbb B\vee F,\ \ \Pi\mathcal I=\mathbb B\wedge F
rows.how: the join and the wedge forms of T both equal the classical sum of (1/2) m |xdot|^2 (the wedge form read as the coefficient of I); dT/dt = Pi = B v F along the motion (power series), and dT/dt = 0 for the free body

rows.paper: F_b=\dot P_b=\mathsf I_b[\dot{\mathbb B}_b]\ \Rightarrow\ m\dot{\mathbf v}_b=\mathbf f_b,\ \ \mathsf I_C[\dot{\mathbf B}_b]=\mathbf T_b;\ \ \mathbf p\cdot C+\mathbf P\mathcal I=\mathbf q\cdot C+\mathbf Q\mathcal I\iff\mathbf p=\mathbf q,\mathbf P=\mathbf Q
rows.ours: I[\dot B] = F\ \Rightarrow\ m\,a = f,\ I_C[\dot A]=T
rows.how: Euler's two laws are the two parts of one equation; the splitting is legitimate because (p, P) -> p.O + P I is injective (rank test)

rows.paper: e^{\alpha\bar B}=1+\alpha\bar B\,(\bar B^2=0),\ \cos\alpha+\bar B\sin\alpha\,(-1),\ \cosh\alpha+\bar B\sinh\alpha\,(+1);\ \ M\widetilde M=(m_\emptyset^2+m_{12}^2+m_{31}^2+m_{23}^2)+2(m_\emptyset m_{0123}-m_{01}m_{23}-m_{02}m_{31}-m_{03}m_{12})\mathbf e_{0123}
rows.how: exact power series for the three exponentials (the cosh case needs a Lorentz-type base, i.e. one generator of the other sign); the Study-number identity on random integer coefficients; and the renormalised motor M/sqrt(M M~) = s(M + d(...)) has M M~ = 1

rows.note: Checked against the classical vdot = -omega x v (independent of the star): e01 and e03 agree with the printed formula; the e02 coefficient is (b03 b23 - b01 b12), whereas the printed one is (-b01 b12 - b03 b23).
rows.how: a body with unit mass and unit principal inertias has I = star exactly (built from point masses with rational positions); the e01 and e03 coefficients of the printed six-multiplication formula are reproduced; the e02 coefficient is (b03 b23 - b01 b12), the printed one has -b03 b23

rows.paper: F_g=-9.81\star(\widetilde M\mathbf e_{02}M)\ \to\ 2(m_\emptyset m_{23}+m_{12}m_{31})\mathbf e_{12}+(1-2(m_{12}^2+m_{23}^2))\mathbf e_{31}+2(m_{31}-m_\emptyset m_{12})\mathbf e_{23}
rows.note: With the rotor M = m0 + m12 e12 + m31 e31 + m23 e23 we find the e23 coefficient 2(m31 m23 - m0 m12); the printed text reads 2(m31 - m0 m12), which looks like a dropped factor m23 (the other two coefficients agree exactly).
rows.how: for unit rotors with rational components: the e12 and e31 coefficients agree with the printed ones; the e23 coefficient is 2(m31 m23 - m0 m12), the printed 2(m31 - m0 m12) lacks a factor m23 (dimensionally the other two terms are quadratic)

rows.paper: \mathsf I_C=\tfrac m{12}\mathrm{diag}(h^2+d^2,\,w^2+d^2,\,w^2+h^2);\ \ C=m\big(\tfrac{h^2+d^2}{12}\mathbf e_{03}+\tfrac{w^2+d^2}{12}\mathbf e_{02}+\tfrac{w^2+h^2}{12}\mathbf e_{01}+\mathbf e_{12}+\mathbf e_{31}+\mathbf e_{23}\big)
rows.note: With w, h, d along x, y, z the exact map sends e23 to m(h^2+d^2)/12 e01, e31 to m(w^2+d^2)/12 e02, e12 to m(w^2+h^2)/12 e03. The printed C lists (h^2+d^2)/12 with e03 and (w^2+h^2)/12 with e01, i.e. in the reverse order; a relabelling of the axes (w along z?) or an index swap. Worth a look.
rows.how: the cuboid is integrated exactly (3x3x3 Simpson weights are exact for quadratics). The map sends the rotation about x (e23) to (m/12)(h^2+d^2) e01.

rows.paper: \dot{\mathbb B}_b=-\epsilon(\mathbf v_b\cdot\mathbf B_b);\ \ \mathbb B_b=\mathbf B_0+\widetilde M_{B_0}(\epsilon\mathbf v_0)M_{B_0};\ \ M=e^{-(\mathbf p/m)t/2}M_0e^{-(\mathbf L_b/i)t/2}
rows.how: free spherical top (a cube): exact series through order 5. With B_0 = L_b / i and p/m = M_0 (eps v_0) M_0~: the two exponentials do not commute and cannot be merged

rows.paper: \mathsf I_C[\mathbf B]=i\mathbf B+(i_3-i)[\mathbf B]_3E_3;\ \ \mathbf A=\mathbf B_0-\mathbf L_b/i=(1-i_3/i)[\mathbf B_0]_3E_3=(i_1-i_3)[\mathbf L_b]_3E_3;\ \ M=M_pM_0M_{L_b}M_A
rows.note: Everything agrees except the last form in (B.14): from A = (1 - i3/i)[B0]_3 E3 and [L_b]_3 = i3 [B0]_3 one gets A = (1/i3 - 1/i1)[L_b]_3 E3. The printed "(i1 - i3)[L_b]_3 E3" is dimensionally off (it probably means inverse inertias).
rows.how: free symmetric top (two equal inertias): (B.7), (B.12), the conserved [B]_3, the closed form of B_b(t) (B.13) and the motor (B.15) all satisfy the free equations as exact series through order 5, also with an initial rotation M_0

rows.paper: \mathsf I_C[\dot{\mathbf B}]=\mathbf B_b\times\mathsf I_C[\mathbf B_b]\ \Rightarrow\ \dot B_{b1}=\omega_1B_{b2}B_{b3}\ (\text{cyclic}),\ \omega_1=\tfrac{i_2-i_3}{i_1};\ \ i_1\ge i_2\ge i_3:\ \omega_2<0
rows.how: exact on random diagonal bodies; energy and |L|^2 conserved; for i1 > i2 > i3 the middle axis has a positive squared growth rate (tennis racket / Dzhanibekov effect), the other two oscillate

rows.paper: j=-(1+\rho)\dfrac{(Q\vee Q\times(\mathbb B_+-\mathbb B_-))\cdot\widetilde N}{(Q\vee Q\times(\mathsf I_+^{-1}[N]-\mathsf I_-^{-1}[N]))\cdot\widetilde N};\ \ \mathbb B_\pm\leftarrow\mathbb B_\pm\pm j\,\mathsf I_\pm^{-1}[N]
rows.note: Exact: with B+ <- B+ + j I+^-1[N] and B- <- B- - j I-^-1[N] (eq 2.33) the restitution law holds when the denominator of j contains I+^-1[N] PLUS I-^-1[N]. In (2.32) the printed denominator has a minus, and the line just above (2.33) writes B_pm - (-+) j I^-1[N]. If the minus comes from an orientation convention for N on the second body, it is worth stating.
rows.how: two random rigid bodies in 3D, a contact point Q and a normal line N = n.Q; V = Q v (Q x B) is the velocity line at Q. Only one reading satisfies the restitution law exactly

rows.paper: Lagrangian derivation I^r I[Bdot] = B x (I^r I[B])
rows.note: needs the dual (reciprocal) algebra used for the scalar-product form of the join; the resulting free equation I[Bdot] = B x I[B] IS checked (F25)

rows.paper: constrained motion: L v F_L = 0 (hinge)
rows.note: not done: a second, longer computation; the building blocks (inertia map, join) are in place

rows.paper: the ganja.js code, the hypercube, the SAT collision test, Euler/RK4 integrators
rows.note: code listings are figures in the PDF; only the equations they implement were checked

rows.paper: closed forms for exp and log of a 3D motor (De Keninck)
rows.note: only given as a figure of code

rows.paper: exercises and solutions
rows.note: D.1, D.2 (2D inertia of a rotation about the centroid and of a translation) are special cases of F20; the rest were not read line by line
